title: Carlos Chagas's birth chart
metaDescription: Carlos Chagas's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 17.0° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Venus holds a conjunction to Uranus at 0.7° — close enough to weld taste to disruption. A conjunction concentrates rather than balances — the pair burns one fuel line.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 17.0° of Cancer is the Sun's exact seat — second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Mars in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Leo (7.7°), Venus in Virgo (2.4°), Mars in Aries (21.0°): thought that arrives already in motion, attraction that grows by reliability, effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Venus and Uranus: 0.7° from an exact conjunction. Two bodies in the same degree are not read as neighbours but as a merger: whatever one wants, the other is already funding. Behind it, Jupiter sextile Neptune at 0.9°, and the Sun square Saturn at 1.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags four placements in this chart. Venus in Virgo at 2.4° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Aries at 21.0° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Pisces at 12.6° is in domicile; Saturn in Aries at 15.5° is in fall. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements earth 4, fire 3, water 2; modalities cardinal 3, fixed 3, mutable 3. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Jupiter was retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Pisces into Aries during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.3° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
